reasons: The cited Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term: professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel (19.1), material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation/specifications (19.1, 19.2), 90 days for Deliverables running from the later of delivery or acceptance and the full subscription term for Hosted Services (19.2, exceeding the 12-month software benchmark), no malicious code and Applicable Law compliance (19.3), and a re-perform/repair/replace plus refund remedy (19.4).

The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual, confined to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty or stated remedy, so there is no risk of the disclaimer swallowing the express warranty or of an 'AS IS' walk-away.
The failed deterministic period check is a false negative caused by the period being spelled in words ('ninety days') rather than digits; the rationale correctly identifies and explains this.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed (rendered text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was generated; retaining this as internal evidence is the correct treatment.
Only minor sub-element gaps exist (malicious code warranty limited to code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor'), which under the classification rules are noted rather than flagged as a deviation.
